subject: Geography
sub_topic: Ocean upwelling — causes, regions and significance

concepts.name: Mechanism of Coastal Upwelling: Ekman Transport and Wind-Driven Dynamics
key_dimensions: Role of Trade Winds / prevailing winds in driving surface water away from coast
Ekman spiral and the 90° deflection rule (Coriolis effect) — common trap: direction differs in NH vs SH
Why upwelling occurs on WESTERN coasts of continents (eastern boundary currents), not eastern coasts
Distinction between upwelling zone depth (thermocline breach) and typical ocean mixing depth

concepts.name: Equatorial Upwelling: Mechanism and Distinction from Coastal Upwelling
key_dimensions: Divergence of surface waters at the equator due to opposing Coriolis deflections (NH vs SH)
Role of Trade Winds blowing westward along the equator — upwelling in eastern equatorial Pacific/Atlantic
Comparison with coastal upwelling: open-ocean vs. nearshore setting
UPSC trap: Equatorial upwelling is strongest in Pacific, but also present in Atlantic and Indian Ocean (seasonally)

concepts.name: Open-Ocean (Divergence) Upwelling and Downwelling Zones
key_dimensions: Upwelling at cyclonic gyres / divergence zones vs. downwelling at anticyclonic gyres / convergence zones
Sub-polar gyres as upwelling zones; subtropical gyres as downwelling zones — trap: subtropical gyres are nutrient-poor deserts
Role of wind stress curl in generating open-ocean upwelling (Ekman pumping)
Significance for deep-water ventilation and thermohaline circulation

concepts.name: Eastern Boundary Upwelling Systems (EBUS): Four Major Regions
key_dimensions: Four canonical EBUS: California Current, Humboldt (Peru) Current, Canary Current, Benguela Current — UPSC trap: which coast/continent each belongs to
Common features: cold SST, arid/desert hinterlands, rich fisheries, persistent fog/low stratus clouds
Comparison: Humboldt vs. Benguela — relative productivity and fish species (anchoveta vs. pilchards)
Why EBUS coasts are arid (cold upwelled water stabilizes atmosphere, suppresses rainfall) — linkage to Atacama, Namib, Sahara coastal deserts

concepts.name: Humboldt (Peru) Current Upwelling System
key_dimensions: Driven by Southeast Trade Winds; Ekman transport directed westward/offshore in SH
World's most productive marine ecosystem — anchoveta fishery, guano deposits (Peru/Chile)
Linkage to El Niño: suppression of upwelling during warm ENSO phase → fishery collapse
UPSC trap: Humboldt Current is a cold eastern boundary current, NOT a western boundary current

concepts.name: Benguela Current Upwelling System and its Climatic Consequences
key_dimensions: Location: west coast of southern Africa (Angola to South Africa); driven by SE Trade Winds
Cold upwelled waters responsible for Namib Desert aridity and coastal fog (advection fog)
Biodiversity hotspot: supports large populations of penguins, seals, seabirds
Trap: Benguela flows northward (cold, eastern boundary) — contrast with warm Agulhas on east coast of Africa

concepts.name: Monsoon-Driven Upwelling: Arabian Sea and the Somali Coast
key_dimensions: Unique case: upwelling driven by SEASONAL monsoon winds, not steady Trade Winds
Southwest Monsoon drives offshore Ekman transport along Somalia and southwest India (Kerala coast)
Somali Upwelling: strongest in the world seasonally — linked to Somali Jet and Great Whirl formation
UPSC trap: Indian Ocean lacks a classic EBUS; its upwelling is monsoonal and episodic, not year-round

concepts.name: Upwelling and Nutrient Dynamics: Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Silica Cycling
key_dimensions: Deep water is nutrient-rich (nitrates, phosphates, silicates) due to biological pump and remineralization
Upwelling brings nutrients to photic zone → triggers phytoplankton blooms
Trap: upwelling waters are also CO2-rich — making upwelling zones both carbon sources AND biological sinks (net balance debated)
Role of iron (micronutrient) in limiting productivity in some upwelling zones (HNLC regions)

concepts.name: Upwelling and Primary Productivity: Phytoplankton Blooms and Food Web
key_dimensions: Upwelling zones cover <1% of ocean surface but account for ~20–50% of global marine fish catch
Trophic cascade: phytoplankton → zooplankton → small pelagics (anchoveta, sardines) → large predators
Chlorophyll-a concentration as a proxy for productivity — detectable via satellite (remote sensing)
Trap: high productivity ≠ high biodiversity — upwelling zones have high biomass but often low species diversity

concepts.name: El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) and its Impact on Upwelling
key_dimensions: During El Niño: weakening of Trade Winds → thermocline deepens → upwelling suppressed in Peru/equatorial Pacific
Consequences: collapse of anchoveta fishery, coral bleaching, drought in Australia/South Asia
During La Niña: enhanced Trade Winds → stronger upwelling → above-normal productivity
UPSC trap: El Niño warms eastern Pacific SST (not western); upwelling suppression is in the EAST

concepts.name: Thermohaline Circulation and Deep-Water Upwelling (Abyssal Upwelling)
key_dimensions: Deep water formed at polar sinking zones (NADW, AABW) must return to surface via slow upwelling
Southern Ocean as the primary site of abyssal upwelling — wind-driven divergence brings old deep water up
Residence time of deep water (~1000 years) vs. upwelling timescale — carbon sequestration implication
Trap: thermohaline upwelling is different from wind-driven coastal upwelling in timescale and mechanism

concepts.name: Upwelling and Oxygen Minimum Zones (OMZs)
key_dimensions: High productivity from upwelling → massive organic matter sinking → bacterial decomposition consumes O2
OMZs form at mid-depths (~200–1000 m) below upwelling zones — Eastern Pacific and Arabian Sea OMZs are most intense
Consequences: hypoxic conditions, denitrification (N2O release), dead zones affect benthic and fish communities
UPSC trap: upwelling creates both productive surface waters AND dead zones below — apparently contradictory

concepts.name: Upwelling and Climate Regulation: Carbon Cycle Implications
key_dimensions: Upwelling brings CO2-rich deep water to surface → outgassing to atmosphere (source)
Simultaneous biological pump: phytoplankton fixes CO2 → sinks as organic matter (sink)
Net flux depends on local balance — eastern equatorial Pacific is a net CO2 source
Climate change scenario: altered wind patterns may weaken upwelling → feedback on global carbon cycle

concepts.name: Fog Formation and Coastal Desert Aridity Linked to Upwelling
key_dimensions: Cold upwelled SST cools overlying air below dew point → advection fog forms over cold current coasts
Fog provides moisture to coastal deserts (Namib, Atacama) sustaining unique fog-adapted ecosystems
Atmospheric subsidence over cold waters suppresses convective rainfall — reinforcing aridity
UPSC trap: Atacama and Namib are among driest places on Earth despite being coastal — upwelling explains this paradox

concepts.name: Seasonal and Temporal Variability of Upwelling
key_dimensions: Seasonal upwelling: Arabian Sea (SW monsoon), Gulf of Guinea (boreal summer trade winds)
Year-round vs. seasonal upwelling — California and Benguela are more continuous; Somali is highly seasonal
Interannual variability driven by ENSO, PDO (Pacific Decadal Oscillation), IOD
UPSC trap: upwelling intensity is not constant — fishery yields vary year to year due to climatic oscillations

concepts.name: Upwelling vs. Downwelling: Comparative Oceanographic and Ecological Significance
key_dimensions: Upwelling: divergence, cold SST, nutrient-rich, high productivity, CO2 outgassing
Downwelling: convergence, warm SST, nutrient-poor, low productivity, carbon/oxygen sequestration into deep
Downwelling zones (subtropical gyres) as ocean deserts — trap: largest ocean zones by area but least productive
Downwelling role in deep-water formation and thermohaline circulation (e.g., North Atlantic Downwelling)

concepts.name: Fisheries, Geopolitics, and Economic Significance of Upwelling Zones
key_dimensions: Peru/Chile (Humboldt) — world's largest single-species fishery (anchoveta for fishmeal/fish oil)
Canary Current — disputed waters off Western Sahara; EU fishing agreements and geopolitical tensions
Benguela — South Africa and Namibia's blue economy; BCLME (Benguela Current Large Marine Ecosystem) Commission
UPSC relevance: EEZ conflicts, sustainable fisheries (SDG 14), food security, and blue economy policy

concepts.name: Climate Change Impacts on Upwelling Systems
key_dimensions: Intensification hypothesis (Bakun, 1990): global warming → stronger land-sea pressure gradients → stronger upwelling winds
Counter-effect: ocean stratification increases → even if winds strengthen, thermocline deepens → less nutrient upwelling
Poleward shift of upwelling zones and associated fisheries under warming scenarios
UPSC trap: climate change effects on upwelling are non-linear and regionally variable — not uniformly positive or negative

concepts.name: Upwelling in the Indian Ocean: Unique Characteristics and Regional Variations
key_dimensions: No classic EBUS in Indian Ocean — upwelling is monsoonal (Somalia, Oman, SW India coast)
West coast of India (Kerala): upwelling during SW monsoon supports Kerala fisheries — sardines, mackerel
Seychelles-Chagos Thermocline Ridge: open-ocean upwelling hotspot in central Indian Ocean
UPSC trap: Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) modulates upwelling off Sumatra/Java coast (eastern Indian Ocean upwelling during positive IOD)
